g1.label: 1. The flat near the station is ___ (cheap) than the flat in the city centre.
g1.why: A short adjective adds -er before than: cheap → cheaper.

g2.label: 2. Online lectures are ___ (convenient) than lectures on campus.
g2.why: Long adjectives take more + adjective before than.

g3.label: 3. Of all the vocabulary apps I have tried, this is the ___ (good).
g3.why: Superlative of good is irregular: good → better → best.

g4.label: 4. Our new flat is not as ___ (quiet) as the old one.
g4.why: In “not as … as” the adjective stays in its basic form.

g5.label: 5. The more I practise, the ___ (easy) it gets.
g5.why: The comparative + the comparative: the more…, the easier.

g6.label: 6. Her presentation was ___ (good) than mine, so her group won.
g6.why: Compare two things with the irregular comparative: good → better.

g7.label: 7. Of the three modules this term, Business English is the ___ (useful).
g7.why: Among three or more, a long adjective takes the most.

g8.label: 8. Prices in Munich are a lot ___ (high) than in Leipzig.
g8.why: A lot + comparative: high → higher, followed by than.

g9.label: 9. This café is the ___ (noisy) place on campus, so I never study there.
g9.why: Noisy ends in -y: change y to i and add -est.

g10.label: 10. Student flats in this city are getting ___ (expensive) every year.
g10.why: More and more + adjective describes a change that keeps growing.

g11.label: 11. This time yesterday, we ___ (look) at flats in the city centre.
g11.why: This time yesterday describes an action in progress: past continuous.

g12.label: 12. Would it be possible ___ move the viewing to Friday?
g12.why: Would it be possible + to-infinitive is a polite request.
